statement: For iid nearest-neighbor bond percolation on the infinite path Z, p_c=1 and theta(p_c)=1. Consequently the assertion theta(p_c)=0 for every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph requires an exclusion of p_c=1.
assumptions: G is the infinite path Z
theta(p)=P_p(0 has an infinite open cluster)

source.basis: Independent elementary derivation; Hutchcroft's primary statement verifies that the intended target already assumes p_c<1.

proof: For p<1, the probability of an open ray of length n in either direction is at most 2p^n, tending to zero. Any infinite component of 0 contains one of the two rays, so theta(p)=0. At p=1 all edges are open, so theta(1)=1 and p_c=1.
remaining_gap: No gap found by w440 in this boundary result; the full P0043 target is not proved.

statement: For every integer n>=1, the supremum of P_{p_c(G)}(o connects to graph distance n) over infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graphs G of maximum degree at most 3 with p_c(G)<1 and roots o is 1. Therefore no graph-independent bound f(n)->0 holds on this class.
assumptions: graph-dependent constants are not ruled out

source.basis: INDEPENDENT.md, uniform L-subdivision of the 3-regular tree

proof: The subdivision T_L has p_c=2^(-1/L). For a branching root and 1<=n<=L, a_L(n)=1-(1-2^(-n/L))^3. For fixed n let L tend to infinity; then a_L(n) tends to 1. At n=L it is exactly 7/8.
remaining_gap: No gap found by w440 in this boundary result; the full P0043 target is not proved.

statement: On the uniform L-subdivision T_L of the 3-regular tree, p_c=2^(-1/L)<1, critical clusters are almost surely finite, critical susceptibility is infinite, and (kL) P_{p_c}(o connects to graph distance kL) tends to 6L at a branching root.
assumptions: L is a fixed positive integer
o is an original degree-3 vertex

source.basis: INDEPENDENT.md, generating-function fixed points, exact recurrence, shell count

proof: Coarse bonds are independent with retention p^L. Critical forward survival u_0=1, u_{k+1}=u_k-u_k^2/4 tends to zero, and reciprocal increments tend to 1/4, giving k u_k->4. The root probability is 1-(1-u_{k-1}/2)^3, giving limit 6 after multiplying by k. Each original shell k has expected connected count 3*2^(k-1)*(1/2)^k=3/2, so susceptibility is infinite.
remaining_gap: No gap found by w440 in this boundary result; the full P0043 target is not proved.

statement: DRAFT source correction, pending independent review. In Hutchcroft's arXiv:1605.05301, the exponential-growth connectivity bound uses finite susceptibility only for p<p_c (Theorem 6). Supermultiplicativity of kappa_p(n)=inf{P_p(x connects to y):d(x,y)<=n}, followed by left continuity of sup_n kappa_p(n)^(1/n), transfers the rate bound to p_c. The proof does not require finite susceptibility at p_c or a branching-random-walk comparison. On the 3-regular tree the critical susceptibility is infinite, so an ordinary finite-critical-susceptibility interpretation of the old C0084 attempt is false. Its undefined qualifier 'spherically averaged' is not treated as a separate established theorem.
assumptions: connected locally finite quasi-transitive graphs of exponential growth for Hutchcroft's rate bound
the old C0084 attempt is unverified concept material
this corrects a source description, not the full P0043 problem

source.source_quote: expected cluster size is finite for every p<p_c
source.old_quote: His proof uses the growth to show that the susceptibility is finite at p_c in a spherically-averaged sense via a comparison with a branching random walk with killing at rate given by the growth

proof: Primary proof uses chi(p)<infinity only below p_c; the exact critical 3-regular tree shell expectation is 3/2 for every radius, so chi(p_c)=infinity. The undefined spherical qualifier is not independently interpreted or certified.
remaining_gap: Independent review pending; no live card revision applied.

statement: For a deterministic finite offspring sequence a_i in {1,2}, parameter 0<p<=1 and terminal depth n, let q_n=1, q_i=1-(1-p q_(i+1))^a_i and m_i=p^i product_(j<i)a_j. Then 1/q_0=1/m_n+sum_(i<n:a_i=2) 1/[4 m_i (1-p q_(i+1)/2)].
proof: The reciprocal difference at a branching index is 1/[4(1-p q_(i+1)/2)], and is zero at a_i=1. Unrolling scales the correction by 1/m_i. AUDIT_W438.md checks indices, endpoints, positivity and independence; 24 exact rational cases agree.
remaining_gap: No gap found in this finite tree identity. A general-graph comparison is not established; w440's designated triad review is separate.
